## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 2/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
State of the art (as of July 2026) in AI coding-agent governance and harness design — the problem space of the claude.md-workflow repo: project instruction files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style), lifecycle hooks, deterministic verification gates, persistent agent memory/working-state across sessions and compaction, behavioral guardrails against scope creep/overclaiming/sycophancy, git-level enforcement, task contracts, and parallel multi-agent orchestration (worktree isolation, orchestrator/reduce patterns, adversarial review). Survey and compare best practices from: Anthropic (Claude Code, Agent SDK, skills/hooks/subagents), OpenAI (Codex, AGENTS.md), Google (Gemini CLI/Jules/Antigravity), Microsoft (GitHub Copilot agents, AutoGen/agent frameworks), NVIDIA (agent toolkits/NeMo), xAI (Grok agents/coding); and non-Western labs: Moonshot AI (Kimi K2.5 agentic training), Zhipu/Z.ai (GLM-5.x coding agents), DeepSeek (agentic/tool-use practices), Tencent (recent Hunyuan model launch and agent tooling), MiniMax (M-series agentic models), Alibaba Qwen if relevant; plus respected independents: Nous Research (Hermes 4/Hermes agent), Fundamental Research Labs (Peter Wang co-founder), the team behind the Ornith-1.0 LLM, tinygrad/George Hotz's approach to minimal harnesses, and any other influential open agent-harness projects (e.g. OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Cline, Devin/Cognition). For each: what they prescribe for instruction-file structure and length, memory persistence, verification/eval gating, multi-agent patterns, and prompt-vs-deterministic enforcement. Identify convergent consensus, notable divergences (especially Western vs Chinese lab practices), and concrete, citable insights that should shape a 2026 rewrite of a drop-in governance kit for coding agents. Note if any named entity cannot be verified to exist (e.g. 'Ornith-1.0') rather than guessing.

## Claim under review
"GitHub's 'Agent Merge' feature implements git-level enforcement of task completion conditions: the agent may drive CI back to green, address review feedback, and merge only when user-specified conditions are met."

**Source:** https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-app-the-agent-native-desktop-experience/ (primary)
**Supporting quote:** "Then Agent Merge helps carry that pull request through review, checks, and merge... You choose how far Copilot should go: drive CI back to green, address feedback, or merge when your conditions are met."

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

# Agent Merge Feature

Yes, the page describes a feature called "Agent Merge."

**Publication Date:** June 2, 2026

**What the article states about Agent Merge:**

"Agent Merge helps carry that pull request through review, checks, and merge. It monitors CI, tracks required reviewers, addresses failing checks, and waits for all conditions to be satisfied. You choose how far Copilot should go: drive CI back to green, address feedback, or merge when your conditions are met. You decide what automation is enabled and what ships."

The description indicates that users have control over the automation scope—determining whether Copilot should resolve CI failures, handle reviewer feedback, or execute the merge itself once conditions are satisfied.

Web search results for query: "GitHub Copilot "Agent Merge" feature pull request CI merge conditions"

Links: [{"title":"Ask @copilot to resolve merge conflicts on pull requests - GitHub Changelog","url":"https://github.blog/changelog/2026-03-26-ask-copilot-to-resolve-merge-conflicts-on-pull-requests/"},{"title":"Fix merge conflicts in three clicks with Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Changelog","url":"https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-13-fix-merge-conflicts-in-three-clicks-with-copilot-cloud-agent/"},{"title":"GitHub Mobile: Fix merge conflicts with Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Changelog","url":"https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-08-github-mobile-fix-merge-conflicts-with-copilot-cloud-agent/"},{"title":"GitHub Copilot Can Now Fix Merge Conflicts in a Pull Request | FettesPS","url":"https://www.fettesps.com/github-copilot-can-now-fix-merge-conflicts-in-a-pull-request/"},{"title":"Assigning and completing issues with coding agent in GitHub Copilot - The GitHub Blog","url":"https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/assigning-and-completing-issues-with-coding-agent-in-github-copilot/"},{"title":"About GitHub Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/agents/coding-agent/about-coding-agent"},{"title":"Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/github-copilot-app/managing-issues-and-pull-requests"},{"title":"Asking GitHub Copilot to make changes to an existing pull request - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/make-changes-to-an-existing-pr"},{"title":"What Makes a GitHub Issue Ready for Copilot?","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2512.21426v1"},{"title":"Best practices for using GitHub Copilot to work on tasks - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/cloud-agent/get-the-best-results"}]

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about GitHub Copilot's "Agent Merge" feature:

## Agent Merge Feature Overview

Agent merge is a feature available at the top of the GitHub Copilot app that will prompt the workspace's Copilot session to read your pull request, fix what is blocking it, and merge it as soon as GitHub allows.

## CI Merge Conditions

The search results indicate that you can mention @copilot in pull requests to fix failing GitHub Actions workflows, and more specifically, the agent works in its own cloud-based development environment where it can make the changes, check that the build and tests still pass, and then push.

Additionally, when resolving merge conflicts, Copilot checks that build, tests, and linting still pass, then pushes the result back to the branch.

## Availability and Permissions

The GitHub Copilot app is available for all Copilot plans. However, the person who created the issue can't be the final approver - you'll need a peer, manager, or designated reviewer to give the green light, which promotes collaboration and ensures unreviewed or unsafe code doesn't get merged.

The search results show that agent merge automates the process of preparing and merging pull requests by having Copilot resolve any blocking issues (like failed CI checks) before attempting to merge.
